Those well-known ones are merely heard of here; it is no wonder. What is a wonder here, O lord of gaṇas, is that they are indeed your own!
Those who constantly cultivate your pair of feet enjoy an abundance of sons, grandsons, wealth, and grain.
Having their lotus-feet honored by hosts of many servants, they obtain pure Fortune that is the enjoyment of kings.
You are the cause of the supreme causes of causes; you alone are forever to be known by knowers of the Veda.
You are that which is to be sought by the primal words, O divine form of the moving and unmoving, beyond the range of words!
The Vedas do not know you according to reality, nor even Brahmā and the others, O stage-manager of the moving and unmoving!
You alone destroy, protect, and create everything; who can describe you in praise, [you who are] ungraspable even by the mind?
I destroy the Daityas, headed by Andhaka and Jalandhara in ancient times, who were struck down by the arrows of your baleful glance;

The wise person who reads this praise composed by me,
the multitudes of obstacles will certainly never torment him.
Whoever reads this sacred praise of Ḍhuṇḍhi in the presence of Ḍhuṇḍhi,

A person, having recited this supreme praise with restrained mind,

Sons, wife, fields, excellent horses, an excellent dwelling,

In the western part of the sacred field is Dehalivināyaka; / he will avert all obstacles for his devotees, of this there is no doubt.
In the north-western direction of the sacred field is the elephant-faced one named Uddaṇḍa; / he constantly punishes even the most violent hosts of obstacles of his devotees.
Always in the northern direction of Kāśī is Pāśapāṇivināyaka; / he binds the obstacle-makers through the devotion of the residents of Kāśī.
At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Varaṇā is the charming Kharvavināyaka; / he makes even the immense hosts of obstacles of the good devotees small.
In the east, indeed, for the protection of the sacred field, is the accomplished Siddhivināyaka; / to the west of Yamatīrtha, he quickly grants perfections to practitioners.
And these eight Vināyakas reside in the outer enclosure of Kāśī; / they drive away non-devotees and grant all perfections to devotees.
And those Vināyakas who protect in the second enclosure / of this Avimukta sacred field, I shall now declare them.
On the western bank of the river of heaven, to the north of Arkavināyaka, / the leader of gaṇas, Lambodara, washes away the mud of obstacles.
To the west of that is Kūṭadanta, north of Durgavināyaka; / destroying difficult afflictions, he constantly protects this sacred field.
Somewhat toward the north-east direction from the leader of gaṇas Bhīmacaṇḍa, / Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa, the leader of gaṇas who protects the sacred field, is to be worshipped.
To the east of Dehalivighneśa, the Vināyaka named Kūṣmāṇḍa / is always to be worshipped with devotion for the pacification of great portents.
In the direction of fire (south-east) from the lord of gaṇas named Uddaṇḍa, / the very renowned Muṇḍavināyaka is to be worshipped by devotees.
His body is in Pātāla; the severed head is located in Kāśī; / therefore that god is sung of in Kāśī as Muṇḍavināyaka.

4.57.m: Having beheld Nāgeśa Gaṇapa, who stands in the direction of the lord of death from the elephant-faced god Uddaṇḍamuṇḍa, one is honoured in the world of the serpents. / Now the lords of obstacles stationed in the sixth enclosure are declared; / merely by hearing their names, perfection arises for men. / In the east is Maṇikarṇa Gaṇapati, who destroys obstacles; / in the southeast stands Āśāvināyaka, fulfilling the hopes of devotees; / in the south is Sṛṣṭigaṇeśa, who indicates creation and dissolution; / in the southwest is Yakṣavighneśa, the supreme remover of all obstacles; / in the west is Gajakarṇa, who brings well-being to all; / in the northwest Gaṇapati Citraghaṇṭa protects the city; / in the north Sthūlajaṅgha allays the sins of the self-controlled; / in the northeast let Samaṅgalavināyaka protect the city of Śiva. / To the north of Yamatīrtha, Mitravināyaka is to be worshipped. / And those Vināyakas who are in the seventh enclosure, them I shall declare: / the five lords of obstacles beginning with Moda, the sixth is Jñānavināyaka, / the seventh is Dvāravighneśa, stationed before the great gateway; / the eighth is Avimuktavināyaka, who removes the multitude of all troubles / for those of bowed minds in my sacred field Avimukta. / Whoever remembers these fifty-six elephant-faced gods, / even though standing in a distant country, upon dying attains knowledge. / The meritorious praise of Ḍhuṇḍhi consisting of the fifty-six elephant-faced gods, / whoever of meritorious soul recites it, to him comes success at every step. / These lords of Gaṇas are all to be remembered anywhere whatsoever; / they protect a man falling into the ocean of great misfortune. / Having heard this most meritorious praise and [revering] these Vināyakas, / one would never be afflicted by obstacles, and is also freed from sins. / Having spoken thus, the god of gods, his heart rejoicing, / consecrated with ritual lustrations by Brahmā and the others, having given them their desires, / having gratified everyone appropriately, skilled in what is proper, / entered the royal residence fashioned by Viśvakarman.

4.57.m: Skanda said: / Thus praised by the blessed Lord, the god of gods, the conqueror of obstacles, / the Vināyaka manifested himself in many forms in this manner. / These are the names of that Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, O jar-born [Agastya], / by reciting which a mortal will attain his desired goal. / There are also other forms of that Lord of Gaṇas, Ḍhuṇḍhi, / worshipped with devotion by devotees, countless by the thousands: / Bhagīratha Gaṇādhyakṣa, Hariścandra Vināyaka, / the Gaṇapati named Kapardin, and likewise Binduvināyaka. / The lords of obstacles beginning with these were established there by individual devotees; / through worshipping them too, all riches arise for men. / Having heard this meritorious chapter with faith, / a man, casting off all obstacles, attains the desired state. / Thus ends the fifty-seventh chapter, entitled 'The Manifestation of Ḍhuṇḍhivināyaka', in the latter half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa in the fourth part of the glorious Skandapurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

4.58.m: Agastya said:
What did Hara do then, Skanda, having gone to Mount Mandara,
when that elephant-faced god too was causing delay?
Skanda said:
Listen, Agastya, to the meritorious narrative now being told by me,
pertaining solely to Vārāṇasī, destroying the whole multitude of sins.
When the elephant-faced god was delaying there in Avimuktaka, the best of sacred fields,
the three-eyed lord [Śiva] promptly looked upon Adhokṣaja [Viṣṇu],
and he was addressed repeatedly with great respect:
"Do not do as those who set out before have done!"
Lord Viṣṇu said:
Effort is to be made by living beings according to their intelligence, strength, and weakness;
yet actions bear fruit depending upon you, O Śaṃkara.
Actions are insentient, and living beings are not independent;

4.58.s: tvaṃ ca tatkarmaṇāṃ sākṣī tvaṃ ca prāṇipravartakaḥ .. 6 ..
4.58.d: त्वं च तत्कर्मणां साक्षी त्वं च प्राणिप्रवर्तकः .. 6 ..
4.58.m: you are the witness of those actions, and you are the instigator of living beings.
Yet such a mindset arises in those devoted to your feet
by which you yourself may say: 'Well performed is this by him!'
Whatever action here, whether small or not small,
succeeds indeed, O Lord of the Mountain, when undertaken with remembrance of your feet.
Even a well-accomplished task, well-executed even with great intelligence,
perishes at that very moment if performed without remembering your feet.
Sent by Śambhu, a good effort is made by me today;
for us who possess the wealth of devotion to you, it is already almost accomplished.
Whatever might be exceedingly impossible to accomplish by one's own intellect, strength, and valour,
that task becomes well accomplished through meditating upon you, O Śiva.

4.58.s: yāṃti pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ye bhavaṃtaṃ bhavaṃ vibho ..
4.58.d: यांति प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ये भवंतं भवं विभो ..
4.58.m: Those who, circumambulating you, O Bhava, go forth, O all-pervading Lord,

4.58.s: bhavaṃti teṣāṃ kāryāṇi purobhūtāni te bhayāt .. 12 ..
4.58.d: भवंति तेषां कार्याणि पुरोभूतानि ते भयात् .. 12 ..
4.58.m: their tasks come before them out of fear of you.
Know, O Mahādeva, that this task is already accomplished beyond doubt;
only an auspicious astrological rising is to be considered for entering Kāśī.

4.58.s: athavā kāśisaṃprāptau na ciṃtyaṃ hi śubhāśubham ..
4.58.d: अथवा काशिसंप्राप्तौ न चिंत्यं हि शुभाशुभम् ..
4.58.m: Or rather, in reaching Kāśī, auspicious and inauspicious need not be considered;

4.58.s: tadaiva hi śubhaḥ kālo yadaivāpyeta kāśikā .. 14 ..
4.58.d: तदैव हि शुभः कालो यदैवाप्येत काशिका .. 14 ..
4.58.m: it is at that very moment an auspicious time whenever Kāśī is reached.
Having circumambulated Śambhu and bowed again and again,
Garuḍa's rider then set forth from Mount Mandara accompanied by Lakṣmī.
Having made Vārāṇasī a guest to his eyes, Viṣṇu then
joyfully fulfilled his title 'lotus-eyed' [Puṇḍarīkākṣa].
At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Varaṇā, Viṣṇu, pure in mind,
washed hands and feet and then took a bath along with his garments.
From that time forth, that sacred ford is called Pādodaka,
because the auspicious feet were first washed there by the yellow-robed Lord.

4.58.s: tatra pādodake tīrthe ye snāsyaṃtīha mānavāḥ ..
4.58.d: तत्र पादोदके तीर्थे ये स्नास्यंतीह मानवाः ..
4.58.m: Those men who will bathe here in that Pādodaka sacred ford,
their sin acquired over seven births quickly perishes.

4.58.s: tatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā dattvā caiva tilodakam..
4.58.d: तत्र श्राद्धं नरः कृत्वा दत्त्वा चैव तिलोदकम्..
4.58.m: A man performing a śrāddha there and offering water with sesame seeds
will deliver seven, and seven, and seven [generations of] his kinsmen.
The kind of satisfaction that is obtained by great-grandfathers at Gayā,

4.58.s: tīrthe pādodake kāśyāṃ tādṛśī labhyate dhruvam .. 21 ..
4.58.d: तीर्थे पादोदके काश्यां तादृशी लभ्यते ध्रुवम् .. 21 ..
4.58.m: that very satisfaction is certainly obtained at the Pādodaka sacred ford in Kāśī.
One who has performed a bath in Pādodaka, who has drunk the water of Pādodaka...
Hell shall never touch the man who gives the water of the Pādodaka sacred ford.
Having sipped the foot-water once at the Viṣṇupādodaka sacred ford,
he will certainly never drink his mother's breast-milk again.
One who bathes a Śālagrāma stone marked with a discus with [water from] a conch
and drinks that water of ablution attains immortality.
If one drinks Viṣṇu's foot-water at the Viṣṇupādodaka sacred ford,
what need is there of that nectar attained after a very long time?

4.58.s: kāśyāṃ pādodake tīrthe yaiḥ kṛtā nodakakriyāḥ ..
4.58.d: काश्यां पादोदके तीर्थे यैः कृता नोदकक्रियाः ..
4.58.m: Those who have not performed water rites at the Pādodaka sacred ford in Kāśī—
their very birth is fruitless, having only the glory of a water bubble.
Having performed his daily rites, Viṣṇu, accompanied by Lakṣmī and Garuḍa,
withdrew that form of his that pervades the three worlds;
and fashioning a stone form with his own hands, Ādikeśava
himself worshipped it, which bestows all perfections and prosperity.
Having worshipped that supreme divine form named Ādikeśava,
a mortal considers Vaikuṇṭha to be the courtyard of his own house.
That spot within the bounds of Kāśī is known as Śvetadvīpa;
men who serve that form dwell verily in Śvetadvīpa.
There is another sacred ford there, named Kṣīrābdhi, in front of Keśava;
having performed water rites there, one would dwell on the shore of the ocean of milk.

4.58.s: tatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā gāṃ dattvā ca payasvinīm ..
4.58.d: तत्र श्राद्धं नरः कृत्वा गां दत्त्वा च पयस्विनीम् ..
4.58.m: Having performed a śrāddha there and given a milch cow
adorned with all prescribed ornaments, a man settles his ancestors in Kṣīroda.
A virtuous person who gives a single cow there with devotion
leads one hundred and one ancestors to the shore of the Kṣīroda, muddy with fresh milk-rice.
And giving many excellent cows there with faith along with priestly gifts,
together with beds and bedding, he settles his ancestors comfortably there, one by one.
South of Kṣīroda there is the peerless Śaṅkhatīrtha;
having gratified the ancestors there too, one is glorified in Viṣṇu's world.
South of that is Cakratīrtha, difficult even for the ancestors to attain;
having performed a śrāddha there as well, one is released from debt to the ancestors.
In its vicinity is Gadātīrtha, which destroys mental agonies on every side;

4.58.s: tāraṇaṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ vai kāraṇaṃ cainasāṃ kṣaye .. 37 ..
4.58.d: तारणं च पितॄणां वै कारणं चैनसां क्षये .. 37 ..
4.58.m: it delivers the ancestors indeed, and causes the destruction of sins.

4.58.s: padmatīrthaṃ tadagre tu tatra snātvā narottamaḥ ..
4.58.d: पद्मतीर्थं तदग्रे तु तत्र स्नात्वा नरोत्तमः ..
4.58.m: In front of that is Padmatīrtha; having bathed there, an excellent man,
having gratified the ancestors according to rule, rejoices like Brahmā.
Right there is the sacred ford of Mahālakṣmī, famed throughout the three worlds,
where Mahālakṣmī herself, who brings joy to the three worlds, bathed.

4.58.s: tatra tīrthe kṛtasnāno dattvā ratnāni kāṃcanam ..
4.58.d: तत्र तीर्थे कृतस्नानो दत्त्वा रत्नानि कांचनम् ..
4.58.m: Having bathed in that sacred ford and given jewels, gold,
and silken garments to brahmins, one is never abandoned by Lakṣmī.
Wherever he may be born, he is prosperous there;
even his ancestors become richly blessed through the majesty of the sacred ford.
There indeed stands the form of Mahālakṣmī, praised by the three worlds;

4.58.s: tāṃ praṇamya naro bhaktyā na rogī jāyate kvacit .. 42 ..
4.58.d: तां प्रणम्य नरो भक्त्या न रोगी जायते क्वचित् .. 42 ..
4.58.m: having bowed to it with devotion, a man never becomes diseased.
Having kept an all-night vigil on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Nabhasya,
and thoroughly worshipped Mahālakṣmī, the observer of the vow obtains the fruit of the vow.
There indeed is the Tārkṣyatīrtha in the vicinity of Tārkṣyakeśava;

4.58.s: tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā saṃsārāhiṃ na paśyati .. 44 ..
4.58.d: तत्र स्नात्वा नरो भक्त्या संसाराहिं न पश्यति .. 44 ..
4.58.m: having bathed there with devotion, a man does not see the serpent of worldly existence.
In front of that is Nārādatīrtha, which destroys great sins,
where Nārada received instruction in the knowledge of Brahman.
A man who has properly bathed there attains knowledge of Brahman;
[since he received it] from Keśava, he is proclaimed there in Kāśī as Nāradakeśava.
Having worshipped the god Nāradakeśava with devotion, a man
never occupies the seat of a mother's womb.
In front of it is Prahlādatīrtha, where Prahlādakeśava resides;
having performed śrāddha and other rites there, one is exalted in Viṣṇu's world.
In its vicinity is the great sacred ford Āmbarīṣa, which destroys evil;
performing water rites there, a man attains freedom from impurity.
Ādityakeśava is to be worshipped to the east of Ādikeśava;
just by seeing him, one is released even from grave sins.
Right there is Dattātreyeśvara sacred ford, and [there is] the primordial Gadādhara;
having gratified the ancestors right there, one attains the yoga of knowledge.
To the east of Bhṛgukeśava is the supreme Bhārgava sacred ford.
A wise man who bathes there becomes intelligent, like the son of Bhṛgu.
And there is Vāmanatīrtha to the east of Vāmanakeśava.
Having worshipped that Viṣṇu, one should reside in the presence of Vāmana.
In front of Naranārāyaṇa is Naranārāyaṇa-tīrtha.

4.58.s: tatra tīrthe kṛtasnāno naro nārāyaṇo bhavet .. 54 ..
4.58.d: तत्र तीर्थे कृतस्नानो नरो नारायणो भवेत् .. 54 ..
4.58.m: A man who has bathed in that sacred ford becomes Nārāyaṇa.
And in front of it is Yajñavārāha-tīrtha, which destroys sin.
From taking a dip there, one obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.
There is a very pure sacred ford named Vidāranārasiṃha.
Bathed there, one tears away the sin accumulated over a hundred births.
And to the east of Gopīgovinda is Gopīgovinda-tīrtha.

4.58.s: snātvā tatra samabhyarcya viṣṇuṃ viṣṇupriyo bhavet .. 57 ..
4.58.d: स्नात्वा तत्र समभ्यर्च्य विष्णुं विष्णुप्रियो भवेत् .. 57 ..
4.58.m: Having bathed there and worshipped Viṣṇu, one becomes dear to Viṣṇu.
To the south of Gopīgovinda is the sacred ford named Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha.

4.58.s: na lakṣmyā tyajyate kvāpi tattīrthaṃ parimajjanāt .. 58 ..
4.58.d: न लक्ष्म्या त्यज्यते क्वापि तत्तीर्थं परिमज्जनात् .. 58 ..

Whatever fruit arises from the final ritual bath of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha,
A hundred times that [fruit comes] from a bath with the water of Pañcanada.
The Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha are means to achieve heaven;
A bath in Pañcanada, lasting up to two ghaṭikās, leads to liberation.
Even coronation to the kingdom of heaven is not approved by the virtuous in such a manner

Better it is, having reached Vārāṇasī, to be a servant of those who sprinkle themselves at Pañcanada,
Than to be elsewhere a king attended by millions of monarchs as servants.
Those by whom no bath was taken in the sin-destroying Pañcanada during Kārttika,
They still dwell in the womb, and will dwell in the womb again.
In the Kṛta age it is called Dharmanada; in the Tretā, Dhūtapāpaka;

Whatever fruit there may be elsewhere from sacrificial and charitable works
Performed throughout a lifetime, that [fruit] arises from bathing in Dharmanada during the month of Ūrja.

4.59.m: There is no sacred ford anywhere on earth equal to Dhūtapāpa,

the autumn has been spent unbroken with that food.
In Ūrja one should eat from leaves; bronze vessels should be avoided with effort.
The vow-keeper who eats from bronze does not obtain the fruit of that vow.
In undertaking the restriction regarding bronze, one should give a bronze vessel filled with ghee.
In Ūrja one should not eat honey, which grants an extremely base rebirth.
Upon giving up honey, one should donate ghee and milk-rice with sugar.
One should avoid oil in Ūrja both in anointing and in eating.
That embodied soul would become a denizen of hell because of anointing oneself and so forth there, O sinless one.

gourds together with black gram, along with ten pieces of gold.

deluded by my very māyā, intent upon doctrines of difference,

Having obtained a ghostly womb, by the command of Kālabhairava,
having dwelt for thirty thousand years in the ocean of sorrow,
they would attain liberation thereafter only by the grace of Viśveśa.
Therefore, hatred should not be directed toward Viśveśa, the Supreme Self,
since there is indeed no expiation for men who hate Viśveśa.
For those vile men here who hate Viśveśa even in their minds,
having died, constantly inhabit Andhatāmisra in the next world.
And those who are intent on reviling Śiva, and those who revile the Pāśupatas,
They are to be known as my enemies; falling into impure hell,

Having obtained the grace of Viśveśa, O sage, I too grant liberation.

This Vārāṇasī, O sage, is to be known as the realm of Paśupati;
therefore Paśupati must be worshipped in Kāśī by those desiring the highest beatitude.
Here, at the Pañcanada sacred ford, Viśveśvara himself bathes
in [the month of] Ūrja, always accompanied by his host, with Skanda and his retinue.
Brahmā with the Vedas and with the sacrifices, Brahmāṇī and the other Mothers,
the seven oceans along with the rivers, bathe in Ūrja at Dhūtapāpa.
Indeed, as many conscious embodied beings as there are in the three worlds,
that many come to bathe in Kārtika at Dhūtapāpa.
For those by whom no bath was taken at Pañcanada upon reaching the auspicious [month of] Kārtika,
the birth of those embodied beings is in vain, like a bubble of water.
The Forest of Bliss is holy; more holy than it is Pañcanada;
even more than that is my presence [there], O great sage Agnibindu.
By this very inference, understand indeed the majesty of Pañcanada,
O greatly wise one, the highest of the highest of all sacred fords;
even hearing of which, a wise man is freed from great sins.

4.60.m: his chest illuminated by the Kaustubha jewel, dressed in yellow silk garments, / possessing the splendor of a deep blue lotus, of very smooth and charming form, / with an attractive lotus shining in the pool of his navel, and lovely pink lips, / with teeth like pomegranate seeds, the sky illuminated by his diadem, / his feet praised by the king of the gods, extolled by Sanaka and others, / his supreme majesty sung of by celestial seers such as Nārada and others, / his mind rejoiced by devotees like Prahlāda and others, / holding the staff of the Śārṅga bow, punisher of all demons, / slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, portender of Kaṃsa's destruction— / that supreme Brahman which is absolute liberation, formless, beyond perception, / which had transformed into a human form for the sake of the devotion of his devotees, / whose form the Vedas knew not, nor was it declared by the Upaniṣads, / and which Brahmā and the other gods had not perceived—he became a guest of the sage's eyes. / Filled with joy, his head bowed to the ground, / that sage Agnibindu of great austerity bowed down to Hṛṣīkeśa. / With palms joined at his head, he praised with supreme devotion / Acyuta, the destroyer of Bali, who was seated upon a broad stone. / There near the Pañcanada, frequented by Mārkaṇḍeya and others, / that Agnibindu with a satisfied mind praised Govinda. / Agnibindu said: / "Om, salutations, O lotus-eyed one, granter of purity both outer and inner! / O Puruṣa with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet! / With a mind free of dualities, I bow to your pair of feet which remove all dualities, / O Viṣṇu, praised by Indra and the gods! / Even the words of Bṛhaspati do not succeed in praising him; / who in this world is capable of praising him? Here, devotion is more powerful. / How can the Lord, the Ruler, who is beyond the reach of the mind and senses, / beyond speech, be praised by people of low intellect like me? / The Lord whom words do not penetrate, whom the mind does not conceive here— / who could have the capacity to praise him who transcends mind and speech?

4.60.m:
By whom can the great majesty of that God be comprehended, / whose breath is the Vedas along with their six auxiliary sciences, their words, and their order of recitation?
Though meditating upon him in the space of their hearts, / Sanaka and the others, whose minds, intellects, and senses are unwearied, do not truly find him.
Though his deeds are sung by the best of sages headed by Nārada, / who have lived as celibates from their childhood, he is not fully comprehended.
Subtle in form, unborn, imperishable, one, the primal, beyond the reach of Brahmā and others, invincible, infinite in power, / eternal, free from disease, formless, having an inconceivable form—who knows you, [both] moving and unmoving, and distinct from the moving and unmoving?
Even each single name of yours, O Hari, O Murāri, when chanted—Mukunda, Madhusūdana, Mādhava— / destroys the sins acquired through births of sinners and confers the great fruit of a mighty sacrifice.
O Nārāyaṇa, O deliverer across the ocean of hell, O Dāmodara, O slayer of Madhu, O four-armed one, / O supporter of the universe, O spotless one, O Janārdana! For those who recite [these], where is rebirth here, and where is fear of death?
Those who always contemplate you in their hearts, O Trivikrama, lotus-eyed one having the splendour of a row of clouds, / whose form is clad in garments glittering like lightning—they too touch your splendour of inconceivable form.
O you marked with the Śrīvatsa, O Hari, O Acyuta, O enemy of Kaiṭabha, O Govinda, whose chariot is Garuḍa, O Keśava, holding a discus in your hand, / O lord of Lakṣmī, O slayer of demons, holding the Śārṅga bow in your hand, nowhere is there any fear for a man who is devoted to you.
Those by whom you have been worshipped, O Blessed One, with tulasī flowers whose divine fragrance surpasses the scent of musk— / all the hosts of gods in heaven richly worship those beings of pure nature with garlands of mandāra flowers.
In whose speech is your desire-granting name, O lotus-eyed one, in whose ears are the sweet-syllabled stories of you, / and upon the wall of whose heart your form is painted—by them the state of the formless king is truly not hard to attain.
Those who continually worship you on earth, O you who recline on Śeṣa, O Lord of Śrī—them the principal deities, the lord of the ancestors, Indra, Kubera,

4.60.m:
Śrī Viṣṇu said: / O Agnibindu of great wisdom, storehouse of great austerities, / choose a boon, [for] I am well pleased; there is nothing that cannot be given to you.
Agnibindu said: / If you are pleased, O Blessed One, O lord of Vaikuṇṭha, O Lord of the Universe, / O beloved of Kamalā, then grant what I request here.
Then, permitted by Hari with a knitting of his brows, that ascetic, / having bowed with a joyful heart, chose a boon from Keśava:
O Blessed One, though all-pervading, remain here in this pool of the Pañcanada / for the welfare of all living beings, especially those desiring liberation.
O Lord of Lakṣmī, this boon must be granted to me without hesitation; / I desire no other boon except devotion to your lotus feet.
Having heard that boon of Agnibindu, Madhusūdana, / the husband of the ocean-born [Lakṣmī], pleased, said, "So be it," for the sake of helping others.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: / O Agnibindu, best of sages, I will certainly dwell here, / pointing out the path to liberation for men possessing devotion to Kāśī.
O sage, I am pleased again; state a boon, and I will give it to you. / You are exceedingly devoted to me; may your devotion to me remain steadfast.
For I was eager to stay here from the very beginning, O storehouse of austerity; / therefore, requested by you, I shall indeed dwell here forever.
Having attained Kāśī, who, if possessed of discernment, would abandon it, unless exceedingly foolish? / Having obtained a priceless ruby, who leaves it behind and seeks glass?
With very little effort here, merely by the spending of this body, / which is inevitably fleeting, where else is there liberation as there is here?
Having exchanged the earthen body worn out by old age here, / would the wise not indeed accept an immortal, godlike body?
Neither by austerities nor by gifts, nor by sacrifices with bountiful dakṣiṇās, / is liberation attained elsewhere as it is in Kāśī by the shedding of the body.
Even yogins engaged in yoga, with their minds restrained, / are not liberated in a single birth; but in Kāśī they are liberated by the shedding of the body.

This alone is the great gift, this alone is the great austerity, / this alone is the supreme vow: that one's body dies in Kāśī.
He alone is wise in the world, he alone has conquered his senses, / he alone is meritorious and fortunate, who does not abandon Kāśī once having reached it.
And I too shall remain here as long as Kāśī remains here, O sage; / even at the cosmic dissolution there is no destruction of it, because it rests firmly upon the tip of Śiva's trident.
Having heard this speech of Viṣṇu, the great sage Agnibindu, / with hair standing on end in joy, said: "I choose another boon again:
O Lord of Lakṣmī, residing here in this auspicious sacred ford Pañcanada under my name, / grant liberation perpetually even to non-devotees as well as to devotees.
Those men who, having bathed here in Pañcanada and gone even to other regions, / have met their death—to them also, indeed, grant liberation.
And those men who, having bathed in Pañcanada, shall worship you— / may Fortune, both moving and unmoving in her two forms, never abandon those men."
The blessed Viṣṇu said: / "So be it, O Agnibindu, here as chosen by you, O sage. / With half of your name, my name shall be combined with me.
My name 'Bindumādhava', celebrated in the three worlds, / shall exist in Kāśī, O sage, destroying streams of great sins.
Those meritorious men who will always worship me here in the holy pool of Pañcanada, / whence is there any fear of mundane existence for them?
Fortune in the form of wealth, and Fortune named Liberation, / always go beside those in whose heart and in Pañcanada I [dwell].
Those who, having reached Pañcanada, have not gladdened the brahmins with wealth, / their wealth weeps, [fearing] calamities soon to befall them.
They alone are fortunate in this world, they alone have accomplished their purpose, / who, having attained my presence, have made their riches mine.
This sacred ford shall have the name 'Bindutīrtha' after your name, / destroying all sins, O Agnibindu, best of sages!

Even having committed thousands of sins through delusion, a man / who bathes in the river of dharma during Ūrja becomes instantly freed from sin.
As long as this body is healthy, as long as the senses are not impaired, / so long should one perform vows, for vows are the fruit of having a body.
By eating only once a day, by eating only at night, and likewise by eating only unasked food, / [and] by fasting, this body, a vessel of impurity, should be thoroughly purified.
Vows such as Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa should be performed with effort; / for by observing vows the impure body attains purity.
When the body is purified by vows, dharma abides firm. / Where righteousness is situated, there [alone] are wealth, desire, and liberation.
Therefore vows should constantly be practiced by men / who desire the fruit of the four goals of life, for they bring the presence of dharma.
If a man cannot always perform vows, / then having reached Cāturmāsya, he should do so with effort:
sleeping on the ground, celibacy, abstention from certain foods, / the rule of eating only once a day and so forth, daily gift-giving according to one's capacity,
listening to the Purāṇas, and furthermore putting their meaning into practice, / keeping a perpetual lamp burning, and great worship of one's chosen deity.
And walking in a place full of abundant sprouts and seeds / should be avoided with care by the wise man for the great increase of dharma.
Those unfit for conversation should not be spoken to by those observing the vow of Cāturmāsya; / silence should always be maintained, or only truth should be spoken.
The one observing the vow should avoid niṣpāva beans, lentils, and kodrava grain; / one must always dwell among pure people; a person not observing a vow must not be touched.
Teeth, hair, clothes, and the like must always be cleaned with care; / an improper thought should never be harbored in the heart by the vow-keeper.
Whatever fruit belongs to a vow-keeper during all the twelve months, / that complete fruit belongs to those who observe the vow of Cāturmāsya.

And if one lacks the capacity for a vow during all four months, / then one should observe vows during Ūrja, if one desires the fruit of a whole year.
Those foolish-minded ones whose Kārtika passes without vows here, / of those swinish souls there shall not be even a speck of merit.
A Kṛcchra, or an Atikṛcchra, or even a Prājāpatya vow, / an exceedingly meritorious person should perform according to capacity when the month of Kārtika arrives.
One should perform a vow on alternate days, or a three-night vow, / a five-night or a seven-night vow, when Kārtika arrives, as a vow-keeper.
Or one should observe a fortnight's vow, or fast for the entire month; / Ūrja should never be rendered barren by any vow-keeper anywhere.
Subsisting on vegetables, subsisting on milk, or subsisting on fruit, / or subsisting on barley food, the vow-keeper should observe when Kārtika has arrived.
A man observing the vow should perform the daily and occasional ritual ablutions during Ūrja; / he should observe celibacy during Ūrja, desiring the fruit of a great vow.
He who spends the month of Kārtika in celibacy, with a pure mind, / by him the entire year has been spent practicing celibacy.
He who completes the month of Kārtika with fasts, / by him even a whole year here has been properly fasted.
